import re
from collections import namedtuple

Token = namedtuple("Token", ["type", "lexeme", "line", "col"])

TOKEN_SPEC = [
    ("FLOAT",    r"\d+\.\d+"),
    ("INT",      r"\d+"),
    ("KEYWORD",  r"\b(?:if|else|while|let|print)\b"),
    ("IDENT",    r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"),
    # TODO 1: a STRING token, a double quote to the next double quote.
    #         Where must it go in this list, and why does it matter?
    ("GE", r">="), ("LE", r"<="), ("EQEQ", r"=="), ("NE", r"!="),
    ("EQ", r"="), ("GT", r">"), ("LT", r"<"),
    ("PLUS", r"\+"), ("MINUS", r"-"), ("STAR", r"\*"), ("SLASH", r"/"),
    ("LPAREN", r"\("), ("RPAREN", r"\)"),
    ("SEMICOLON", r";"), ("NEWLINE", r"\n"), ("SKIP", r"[ \t]+"),
    ("COMMENT", r"#[^\n]*"),
    ("MISMATCH", r"."),
]
MASTER = re.compile("|".join(f"(?P<{n}>{p})" for n, p in TOKEN_SPEC))

def tokenize(source):
    line, line_start = 1, 0
    for m in MASTER.finditer(source):
        kind, lexeme = m.lastgroup, m.group()
        col = m.start() - line_start + 1
        if kind == "NEWLINE":
            line += 1; line_start = m.end()
        elif kind in ("SKIP", "COMMENT"):
            continue
        elif kind == "MISMATCH":
            yield Token("ERROR", lexeme, line, col)
        else:
            yield Token(kind, lexeme, line, col)

CASES = [
    ('let x = 1;',              "the baseline: should scan cleanly"),
    ('let s = "hi there";',     "needs STRING; without it, watch it shatter"),
    ('if x != 1 print x;',      "!= must stay one token"),
    ('let n = 3.14;',           "a float is ONE number token"),
]

for src, note in CASES:
    print(f"\n{src!r}   ({note})")
    for t in tokenize(src):
        flag = "   <-- ERROR" if t.type == "ERROR" else ""
        print(f"    line {t.line} col {t.col:2}  {t.type:9} {t.lexeme!r}{flag}")
description: See how a lexer yields ERROR tokens instead of halting when a token pattern is missing from TOKEN_SPEC.

steps.description: `TOKEN_SPEC` defines the lexer rules for numbers, keywords, identifiers, operators, whitespace, comments, and `MISMATCH`, with a placeholder on lines 11-12 where the `STRING` rule is not yet added.

In `tokenize(source)`, instead of raising `SyntaxError` on `kind == "MISMATCH"`, lines 32-33 `yield Token("ERROR", lexeme, line, col)` so the scanner continues past unrecognized characters and reports every token on the line.

Look at line 33: because `MISMATCH` uses `r"."`, each unrecognized character consumes one character of input, emits `Token("ERROR", lexeme, line, col)`, and lets `MASTER.finditer` resume at the very next character.
`CASES` tests four inputs: `'let x = 1;'`, `'let s = "hi there";'`, `'if x != 1 print x;'`, and `'let n = 3.14;'`. It flags any `t.type == "ERROR"` with `<-- ERROR`.

steps.answer: The opening `"` falls through to `MISMATCH` (`ERROR '"'`). Then `hi` and `there` match `IDENT` (`IDENT 'hi'`, `IDENT 'there'` with the space skipped by `SKIP`). The closing `"` matches `MISMATCH` again (`ERROR '"'`).
steps.question: Without a `STRING` entry in `TOKEN_SPEC`, what sequence of tokens does `tokenize('let s = "hi there";')` emit when it reaches `"hi there"` at column 9?

steps.description: While scanning `'let s = "hi there";'`, the opening quote `'"'` at column 9 reaches `kind == "MISMATCH"` and yields `Token('ERROR', '"', 1, 9)` on line 33.
